summary: Object Stamp Flow carded from the MPI-562 brainstorm: SAM3 text extract, a box step for placement, a Krea2 detail pass. Reuses the existing box step kind, so it is descriptor plus workflow only.

Compact plan attached, investigation inline. UI half confirmed free: box and fields step kinds both already exist and SAM3_Detect is already in shipped workflows. One fork found and written into the plan: aspect-preserving fit into the box is NOT expressible in the current node set (MpiFromBox gives w/h/x/y but core has no min-scale node), so this may need one new MpiNode plus a node_lock pin - which changes the size of the card. Decide it on the bench before building downstream.

Starting the Object Stamp flow. Plan's one fork - aspect-preserving fit into the box - is CLOSED with no new node: ImageResizeKJv2 keep_proportion='resize' is literally ratio = min(width/W, height/H), it carries the mask through the same scale, and comfyui-kjnodes is already pinned. Confirmed present in the SHIPPED engine via /object_info on 48188 (IMAGE, width INT, height INT, MASK out; mask optional in). So no MpiFitInBox, no /mpi-nodes-sync, no node_lock bump - the card stays descriptor + workflow, its original size.

STOPPED BEFORE BUILDING - the card's architecture is superseded and nobody ever answered the board question. MPI-621/brief.md names MPI-596 outright: 'SAM3 extract -> fit in box -> Krea2 denoise blend is cut, paste, repair: the same architecture disproven here', and MPI-621/plan.md parks it under 'Noticed, not actioned' as a board question for close-out that was never resolved - so the card stayed a ready todo describing a route measured worse. blending-into-a-photo.md agrees and names this card twice. Evidence: a localised crop/stitch re-grades the patch (ring 10-23 across four model configs) where whole-image-relight-then-composite-back scores 0.91/1.13; and a paste can never occlude - Draw It In's single Klein 9B edit put a leg BEHIND the tiger in 15s, which the disproven 55-node paste route could not do in 38s. Klein already chains 3 ReferenceLatent nodes with Input_Image_2/3 exposed (2 refs ~30s), so 'target + reference + instruction' is buildable today and is the project's stated LoRA-free bet. Counter-evidence kept: a re-render is NOT a paste, so pixel-exact identity of the user's own object is the one thing the carded route buys and the reference route does not - that is the real question, not the graph. Krea2 two-ref is separately ruled out for this: editing.md measures identity and direction as unobtainable together, and nothing on that graph is spatially selective. Three routes put to Fabio; awaiting his call before any build.

DESIGN REDECIDED by Fabio, and first live finding. Design: stage 1 takes target + object; stage 2 is a real transform gizmo (place/scale/rotate, the History Place tool's own ShapeManager 'place' mode) that STAMPS the object onto the target; the edit model then gets the stamped composite and is told to make it real. The stamp is CONDITIONING, not output - which is why this is NOT the paste architecture MPI-621 disproved (there the paste was the final placement with only cosmetic repair, so it could never occlude; here the model re-renders the region and can put foreground over the object). It also collapses the precision worry: the model repairs rather than invents. Topology is Draw It In's 35 nodes unchanged, with 'the drawing' swapped for 'the placed object'. Agreed ladder, one question per rung: (1) stamped composite alone, (2) + clean object as Input_Image_2 if fine detail drifts, (3) + original as Input_Image_3. App ALREADY wires all three (kleinEdit mediaInputs, 2/3 optional), so every rung is testable with no build - Fabio is testing prompts in the app now. FINDING 1 (live, first plate): BiRefNet is SALIENCE segmentation, not SEMANTIC - on a gun-and-knife-on-cloth source it returned all three, because they are one foreground arrangement. Not a threshold or model-quality problem. Fix Fabio specified: stage 2 carries a Remove Background button PLUS an erase/restore brush, so the model does the precise part (it nailed the gun's silhouette) and the human does the semantic part (wiping two big leftover blobs, which needs no precision). Design rule: keep bgMask and userMask as TWO layers composited at dispatch, never flattened, or toggling Remove Background destroys the user's erasures; and the brush must work with the toggle OFF too, for sources BiRefNet whiffs entirely. This grows stage 2 beyond the 'one component, one line' estimate - it is place gizmo + bg toggle + add/subtract alpha brush + UndoStack - but every piece already exists and it still returns ONE composited RGBA through the existing STEP_MEDIA adapter. Also noted: a step today sees exactly one media (out.find(m => m.role === step.role), in both _buildStepSlide and _deriveRunMedia), so a place step on image1 cannot see image2 - needs a `sourceRole` on the step declaration, mirroring the existing `mediaRole` that routes a kind's OUTPUT elsewhere. Card acceptance 2-5 are all superseded; rewrite pending the prompt results.

FINDING 2 - CONCEPT PROVEN LIVE, first plate. Fabio ran it in the app on Flux.2 Klein 9B: a white mug placed on a sunlit coffee table came back grounded, with a contact shadow and the window's warm light picked up on the correct side. So the target + stamp + object route works and the flow is worth building. SLOT ORDER HE USED IS NOT THE ONE I PROPOSED, and the difference is load-bearing: slot 1 = the CLEAN scene, slot 2 = the pixel stamp, slot 3 = the object on no background. Slot 1 is the sampler's source latent, so this config has the model GENERATING the object from scratch guided by refs 2/3, not repairing a paste. Invisible on a plain white mug (nothing to get wrong); predicted to be the worst possible config for a LOGO, since it redraws letterforms every run. If the logo test fails, swap slot 1 to the STAMPED composite before touching the prompt - that is rung 1 vs rung 3, and the logo is the case that separates them. PROMPT: his working prompt was 'Add the object from image three to the scene from image one using image two as a reference for location.' Two defects found - 'reference for location' undersells the stamp, which carries position, scale AND orientation (scale is otherwise free to drift); and 'add the object to the scene' is the wrong verb for a logo, which is applied to a SURFACE, not added to a scene. Fixed by a conditional surface clause, the same device the proven shadow-physics clause uses: solid object -> contact shading; lies on a surface -> follow its curvature, perspective and texture. Explicit 'image one/two/three' slot references are FINE to bake, because the flow fixes the slots - the baked half names slots, the user's optional field carries intent. OPEN: his plates are 1024x1024, about Klein's own normalise target, so the whole-image re-render cost is invisible at this size and will not be until a real 4000x3000 photo. Asked him to diff a region far from the cup to settle whether crop/stitch is required rather than optional.

FINDINGS 3-5, all live on Flux.2 Klein 9B, kleinEdit op, 1024x1024 plates. (3) THE STAMP IS A PLACEMENT HINT, NOT A PASTE - a 2D transform cannot RE-PROJECT. A gun photographed from one camera angle cannot be made to sit correctly on a table seen from another by any translate/scale/rotate/stretch; stretching only destroys the object. So the prompt must split GEOMETRY (free: viewing angle, foreshortening, how it rests) from IDENTITY (locked: design, shape, markings, text, colours, materials). Same shape as Draw It In's 'the scribble is where and how big, not an outline the render stays inside'. TWO CONSEQUENCES: a perspective/warp gizmo is DEAD - translate/scale/rotate is enough, which ShapeManager 'place' mode already does; and the stage-2 hint copy is load-bearing, because Fabio spent real effort on 'the best I could do with stamping', i.e. the surface taught him it was a paste. (4) A LONG PROMPT BREAKS IT, AND THE CAUSE IS LICENCE BUDGET, NOT LENGTH. My ~200-word prompt returned a hugely oversized cup. Cause: 'roughly where' + 'approximately the position and size' + an explicit angle freedom + a gravity freedom COMPOUNDED into 'do what you like', and scale went with them. Fabio's single 'rough' in a 13-word prompt costs nothing because nothing competes with it. Root reason the Draw It In prompt can be long and this one cannot: THERE the geometry is enforced mechanically by crop + stitch-back-only-the-box, so the prompt only handles appearance; HERE there is no crop and no mask, so words were asked to enforce geometry, which they are bad at. That is a direct argument for the shipped flow carrying the crop/stitch rather than treating it as optional. (5) THE LOGO CASE PASSES, and it was the predicted-hardest one. Google logo stamped onto a plain mug came back PRINTED ON and correctly wrapped to the cylinder, letterforms intact, with NO surface-conforming clause in the prompt - Klein already knows how to project a graphic onto a curved surface, it only needs telling where. TWO OF MY PREDICTIONS WERE WRONG: the logo did NOT need the stamped composite in slot 1 (clean scene in slot 1 preserved the letterforms fine), and front-loading the proven Draw It In guardrails was backwards - each of those clauses exists because a specific bug appeared, so they must be added ONE AT A TIME on evidence. CURRENT BASELINE PROMPT (Fabio's, works on mug + logo): 'Add image three to image one using image two as a rough reference for location.' Slots: 1 = clean scene, 2 = pixel stamp, 3 = object on no background. Open: the GUN is the only case that needed an angle licence, so the likely shipping instruction is that sentence plus 'Adjust its angle to fit the scene.' - to be tested on the gun plate next.

FINDINGS 6-7, and the prompt has converged. (6) WHY THE SAME PROMPT WON ONE TEST AND LOST THE OTHER - the two tasks differ in whether anything BOUNDS the scale. A logo applied to a mug is bounded by the mug's own face, so extra licence in the prompt has nowhere to go and costs nothing; a cup dropped onto a table is free-standing, nothing bounds it but image two, so the moment the prompt hedged with 'approximately' the scale drifted and returned a giant cup. Same root cause as finding 4 one level up: PROMPTS ARE BAD AT GEOMETRY, and whatever constrains geometry MECHANICALLY makes the wording stop mattering. A surface does it for the logo; a crop would do it for everything. PREDICTION TO BANK: with InpaintCropImproved sized from the placed bbox, a too-large object physically cannot fit the region, so scale is bounded by the graph rather than by an adjective - the longer prompt should therefore stop breaking the free-standing-object case once cropped, giving ONE prompt that serves both. Untested; it can only be tested inside the flow's real graph. (7) SHIPPING PROMPT CANDIDATE, judged best by Fabio across the mug, logo and gun plates: 'Add image three to image one using image two as a rough reference for location. Adjust its angle to fit the scene.' That is his own 13-word baseline plus ONE clause, added because the gun was the only plate whose viewpoint the stamp could not state. No shadow clause, no glow guard, no 'change nothing else', no identity clause - none has been earned by an observed failure yet, and finding 4 says adding them speculatively is what broke scale. METHOD NOTE for whoever builds this: every run in this session was WHOLE-IMAGE on 1024x1024 plates through the History workspace, which is NOT the configuration the flow ships. Further wording tuning in that configuration measures something that will not exist. The remaining unknowns - crop sizing, whether the richer prompt is safe once bounded, whether shadows clip at the return-region edge - are graph-shaped and need the real flow to answer.

FINDINGS 8-11. PROMPT AND REFERENCE CONFIG ARE NOW SETTLED; the gun angle is the only open failure. (8) VENDOR PROMPTING RULES, researched after Fabio challenged that I was inventing prompt craft rather than reading it (he was right). Sources: docs.bfl.ml FLUX.2 image editing, fal.ai Klein prompt guide, deAPI 'Prompting FLUX.2 Klein'. Rules that actually changed the work: (a) PROMPT LENGTH IS A BAND, roughly 40-120 words - fal says over 100 creates confusion, deAPI says under 40 under-drives the Qwen3 encoder. My 200-word prompt was over (this is the measured cause of the giant cup); Fabio's 13-word one was under. Target 60-90. (b) IDENTITY IS FREE FROM THE REFERENCE while the model is COPYING - refs retain 'exact proportions, dial markings and case finish' and the prompt is meant to spend its words on POSITIONING AND LIGHTING only. So 'keep its design and markings' is wasted budget - EXCEPT once you license a redraw, when it must come back. (c) MORE THAN 3 REFERENCE IMAGES CAUSES IDENTITY MIXING - we were at exactly 3 when we got the duplicated gun. (d) numbered image references are the documented pattern (Fabio was right, I had dropped them). (e) content nouns outweigh modifiers, which is why hedges like 'approximately' both fail to constrain AND dilute. (f) below 768px quality drops, optimal 1024-1536 - consistent with cropping then resizing to 1024. CAUTION ON ONE RULE: the guides say negative/prohibitive phrasing is ignored, but MPI-567 MEASURED the opposite on this exact model (asking for a shadow produced a lit dust cloud; forbidding glow cured it). Our measurement wins on our graph; the word-budget argument alone justifies dropping the guards until a glow actually appears. (9) SHIPPING PROMPT, ~75 words, in band, all positive, two references: 'Place the object from image two into the scene of image one, at the position and size it has in image two. Rest it naturally on the surface it touches, at an angle that matches the camera in image one. Light it with the scene's own light, matching direction, colour temperature and contrast, with contact shading where it meets the surface and a shadow consistent with the shadows already in the scene. Keep everything else in image one unchanged.' CONFIG: slot 1 = clean scene, slot 2 = stamped composite. Two refs, not three. This is the first prompt to pass the logo-on-mug AND the free-standing-cup cases together. MY PREDICTION THAT THE CROP WOULD BE WHAT UNIFIED THEM WAS WRONG - getting into the word band and dropping to two references did it with no crop at all. (10) THE GUN ANGLE IS NOT A PROMPT PROBLEM. A 'Redraw the object ... seen from that scene's camera angle' variant left it at the identical flat product-shot viewpoint. Reason: the stamp IS a picture of the object at the wrong viewpoint, sitting in the conditioning - no wording overrides a picture. (11) SO THE TWO MODES ARE A REFERENCE CONFIG, NOT TWO PROMPTS. Fabio's call is that the user chooses. Exact placement = ref is the STAMP (position, scale, angle all from it; correct whenever the source angle already works, which covered mug, logo and most product shots). Free angle = ref is the CLEAN OBJECT with no stamp, so nothing anchors the wrong viewpoint and location is carried in words - loses precision, gains re-render freedom. It CANNOT be done by adding the object as a third ref: that is the identity-mixing limit from (8c) and it is what produced two guns. NOTE the trade Fabio named (rotation vs scale) has never been observed - the scale blowout was the 200-word budget failure, not a rotation cost. Third answer, likely the strongest and needing no new UI: re-angle the object with a Klein edit in History BEFORE stamping ('show this pistol lying flat, seen from above at 30 degrees'), which changes the pixels instead of arguing with them, and keeps one dispatch. STILL UNTESTED: the tight-crop run against the ~200px anchor threshold. Deferred to the bench during the build, since crop sizing is graph work anyway.

FINDING 12 + CARD REWRITTEN TO THE SETTLED DESIGN. (12) KLEIN 4B TESTED AND FAILED - this is a 9B-ONLY flow, the same call Draw It In made. Carry its modelParams shape: the CLIP arm moves WITH the checkpoint (9B needs qwen_3_8b_int8_convrot; 4B's encoder dies with a shape error that reads as a sampler bug, MPI-600) and Input_Edit_Clip.clip_name needs the dotted form while Input_Edit_Model stays plain. FINAL DESIGN, Fabio's, confirmed back to him: stage 2 is a canvas + 1:1 box + an Auto/Manual toggle defaulting to Auto, plus Remove Background and an erase/restore brush in BOTH modes. AUTO shows the object itself (user moves/scales/rotates it), no prompt box, and dispatches clean scene + stamped composite. MANUAL shows an EMPTY box with NO rotation handle and reveals a prompt box, and dispatches cropped scene + clean object at full frame. The canvas differs because the MECHANISM differs - in Auto the object's pixels are really used so the user sees them; in Manual only the region is used, so a rotation handle would be a lie. That is what makes this better than the rotation toggle we circled for an hour: the UI cannot promise what the mode cannot deliver. The two modes are the identity-vs-viewpoint trade made explicit - Auto keeps the object and its viewpoint, Manual buys the viewpoint by spending exact identity (measured: a pose-described run returned a beautifully lit pistol that was NOT the user's Glock, because a redraw is novel view synthesis and the model has no 3D model of that object). Krea2's editing.md reached the same conclusion independently, making it a model-class property. Auto-placement mode REJECTED: it would duplicate what History already does with a 2-image Klein edit, and the box is the flow's reason to exist. brief.md, plan.md, prompts.md and all 16 acceptance items rewritten; the two dropped designs are recorded in brief.md so nobody re-proposes them.

FINDINGS 13-16, from 14 bench runs on the standalone 8188 bench. The graph is authored and proven, and the crop question is SETTLED - but not the way the plan expected. (13) THE TOPOLOGY TRANSFERS WHOLE. flow_draw_it_in.json was patched, not rebuilt: composite -> InpaintCropImproved -> Klein 9B edit -> ColorMatch -> InpaintStitchImproved all survive, as do the six Input_Lora_Phase1_* slots (193->198 into CFGGuider.model), the 9B checkpoint, qwen_3_8b_int8_convrot, flux2-vae, cfg 1 and 4 steps. The ONE structural change is the second reference: a new ReferenceLatent chained after 108, so conditioning passes 104 -> 108 (image one) -> 203 (image two) -> CFGGuider.positive. First run on the first plate was already good. (14) THE REAL LAW IS FRAMING, NOT CROP SIZE - and it is what made every early run fail. EVERY reference must be framed like the OUTPUT frame. Auto's slot 1 read as 'the clean scene' at FULL FRAME while the output frame was a crop, and the model did exactly what it was told: it painted that whole wide scene into the narrow frame, and the patch stitched back as a MINIATURE ROOM inside the table - sofa, vase, second table, visible seam. Cropping the clean scene to the SAME region with a second InpaintCropImproved (same box, same context factor, image=Input_Image) removes it completely. Proven as a clean A/B on the mug plate: mismatched = doll's house, matched = a mug sitting on the table with a correct contact shadow, correct scale, matching sun direction and no seam. Draw It In never met this because it has ONE reference and that reference IS the crop. (15) CROP SIZE IS NOT A CORRECTNESS KNOB. Once the references are matched, every crop tested worked: 155px, 300px, 384px, 414px, 480px, 607px and full frame. The earlier catastrophic failures at 336/384/480px were the framing mismatch, not tightness - re-run matched, the same sizes are fine. So Draw It In's 4.267 constant TRANSFERS as a sane default (it pins the object near 240px in the edit frame) but it is a quality dial, not a guard. More object pixels visibly helps a SMALL object: at 90px placed, full-frame lost the grip to light grey, while a 155px crop (object at ~731px) came back black and correct. Shadows did not clip at the return edge in any run - mask_blend_pixels 32 held even on a 103px box. (16) ColorMatch is INERT on a modern plate: mean delta 0.032/255, max 9, 0.32% of pixels above 3. It neither caused nor fixed the colour drift seen on some runs. Keep it for the vintage case Draw It In needed it for, but it is not what makes this flow work. Colour fidelity on the object itself still wanders run to run (the same gun came back black at one crop size and tan at another) - NOT settled, and worth a sweep when the app-side wiring is done. Bench-only deviations, not to be carried into the shipped graph: MpiClearVram dropped and the seed pinned so an A/B differs only by what is under test. Proven graphs saved as graph-bench-auto.json and graph-bench-manual.json in this workspace.

FINDINGS 17-19: THE CUT-OFF OBJECT, and it changes the recommended crop config. Fabio spotted a gun sliced clean through the grip in the bench outputs. (17) THE STITCH MASK IS THE CONTRACT, AND A PROMPT CANNOT REACH IT. InpaintStitchImproved writes back ONLY the mask - the box, plus mask_expand_pixels and the blend band - while the model's canvas is the whole CROP, which is bigger. Anything Klein draws outside the box is discarded, producing a dead-vertical cut at box+6px through both the object and its shadow. Auto never showed it because the stamp pins the object's size, so the object is inside the box by construction (verified with a box overlay on big_crop414, small_crop155, mug_matched - all clean). Manual has nothing pinning size, so Klein drew the gun to fill the crop and lost the grip. (18) THE PROMPT LEVER WAS TESTED AND REJECTED - Fabio proposed adding a clause telling the model to keep the whole object in frame. Added as ONE clause on measured evidence, exactly as prompts.md requires: 'Show the object whole, its entire outline inside the frame, sized so it sits clear of the edges.' It changed the render (2.2% of pixels) and did NOT fix the slice - the gun came back cut in the same place. The reason is structural: the model already IS keeping the object whole inside ITS frame, which is the crop; the loss happens downstream in the stitch, which the model knows nothing about. No wording can fix a geometric mismatch, so do not re-attempt this. Row added to prompts.md's 'does NOT work' table. (19) THE FIX IS GEOMETRIC AND IT IS ONE RULE FOR BOTH MODES: make the model's canvas equal the region written back. Pin context_from_mask_extend_factor to 1.0 and grow the write-back with mask_expand_pixels at about 30% of the box side (83px on a 276px box, 52px on a 172px box). Slicing then cannot happen by construction, and the margin is also what gives a cast shadow room to run - the mug's shadow previously ended exactly at the box edge and now continues past the corner cleanly. Proven in both modes: manual_f10_expand83 (whole gun, correct pose from the user's words) and mug_f10_expand52 (whole mug, free shadow). THIS SUPERSEDES finding 15's advice to ship Draw It In's 4.267 constant as the default - 4.267 sizes the CROP, which is now pinned at 1.0, so the constant has no job left in this flow. The saved graph-bench-auto.json / graph-bench-manual.json carry the proven config. App-side note: mask_expand_pixels is an INT input, so the 30% should be driven from MpiMaskSquareBbox.size through an MpiMath rather than hard-coded.

summary: STAGE SPLIT SHIPPED. MpiStepPlace split into MpiStepCutout (the `cutout` kind, stage 2 on image2: Remove Background + Erase/Restore + UndoStack, no gizmo) and a stripped MpiStepPlace (the `place` kind, stage 3 on image1: ShapeManager + Auto/Manual). Both registered in stepKinds.js. Frame seam added: _buildStepSlide now hands a step `sourceValue` beside `source`, and _deriveRunMedia resolves `sourceRole` too. ONE APPROVED DEPARTURE from the drift note: it said composePlacedObject should keep rebuilding from its own value alone, reading the cutout masks out of that step`s value - which would copy both base64 mask layers into place`s snapshot as well, two copies that can disagree. Instead the masks stay in the ONE step that owns them and _deriveRunMedia hands `place` the object as the run will see it (the cutout step`s derived file when that step did anything, the user`s upload when it did not). Two consequences, both measured: `place` in MANUAL derives NOTHING at all (the clean object is already image2), and STEP ORDER IS NOW LOAD-BEARING - declare cutout before place or stage 3 stamps the uncut object. Verified live on an own app:isolated instance (54197, killed by PID lineage; curl :3000 re-checked 200). Every pre-split measurement reproduced: composite law pixel-exact, toggle off/on preserves erasures, undo per-gesture (4148 -> 2074 -> 0, button disables), Auto stamp at the 512x512 SCENE frame, param {172,72,256,256}. NEW: an untouched cutout derives NULL and reports nothing on mount so image2 reaches the run as supplied, Reset returns it to skipping, and the sourceValue seam measured end to end - erasing one quadrant in stage 2 leaves stage 3 with ratio 0.750 of its object pixels. 747/747 tests, lint clean, 0 console errors. user-ux gate still OPEN: no FlowDef declares either kind, so Fabio has still seen none of it.

note: validation.md gains the split section - every pre-split figure reproduced against the pair, plus the skip path and the sourceValue seam (ratio 0.750) measured for the first time.

USER-UX GATE LARGELY CLOSED. Fabio ran the flow in the app: both routes (Auto and Manual) worked, and he separately confirmed stage 2 by hand - remove background, delete pixels, bring pixels back, and undo. First time this card has been seen through the app rather than the bench. TWO FINDINGS, both actioned. (1) ALT-rotate was UNDISCOVERABLE: the gesture is ALT + drag a HANDLE (a bare ALT-drag does nothing - MpiStepPlace mousedown needs a shape.hitTest hit) and it is AUTO-ONLY, and nothing in the UI named it; the place hint now names it plus Shift-to-lock and says why Manual has neither. (2) The prompt field renders in Auto where prompts.md specified Manual-only - a deliberate deviation, and NOT inert: node 18 concatenates Input_Positive onto whichever instruction the switch picked, so the words land in both modes. The real fault was the COPY: the placeholder led with a pose example, which only buys anything in Manual because in Auto the stamp already pins the viewpoint.
